data.title: Wall St Week Ahead-'Black Friday' brings consumer spending into focus for AI-rocked market
data.description:
* Anthropic IPO, solid Nvidia ( NVDA ) earnings fail to lift market

* Holiday retail sales seen up 4.2%, per Oxford Economics

* Consumer spending in focus in light of higher prices, energy costs

By Lewis Krauskopf

NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Investors next week will focus on consumer spending, looking for evidence that a broadly solid economy can help calm a US stock market unsettled by doubts about the AI trade.

The S&P 500 and the Dow tumbled on Friday, confirming they were in a correction, while Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut that had raised hopes of easing worries about an AI trade already roiled by valuation concerns.

Next week, "Black Friday" heralds the onrush of the holiday shopping season as retailers offer a wave of discounts. Investors will watch for signs of how consumers are coping with inflation, including rising energy and borrowing costs. Consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of the US economy.

"If you continue to see a strong consumer, it should help to lift the economy," said Jim Baird, chief investment officer with Plante Moran Financial Advisors. "That directly contributes back to stronger corporate revenue and earnings growth, and provides a catalyst for investors that extends beyond the AI trade and to other parts of the economy."

Investors are still digesting a steep pullback in heavyweight technology and AI stocks.

This week, the blockbuster market debut from Claude creator Anthropic and a solid quarterly report from beleaguered AI chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ) failed to steady the stock market. Spurred by concerns about heavy financing needs and political pushback, doubts have emerged about the massive spending on data centers and other AI infrastructure that has underpinned the 4-year-old bull market.

"Markets and investors are looking at the tech sector with a lot more questions," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest Wealth Management.

The Anthropic IPO offered investors their first chance to invest in a publicly traded AI lab, and the stock's performance was expected to drive broad sentiment in coming days. Anthropic's shares opened sharply higher on their first day of trading, then pared gains and closed up 17% on Thursday, while major stock indexes sank. On Friday, Anthropic fell 9%.

The S&P 500 has fallen 11.6% from its October 6 all-time high, dragged down by the technology sector, which has slumped nearly 24.7% in that time.

A recent series of technology snafus that disrupted areas from banking to travel to email also left investors edgy heading into a US trading week that will be shortened due to the Thanksgiving holiday.

SOLID OCTOBER RETAIL SALES SETTING HOLIDAY TONE?

Weakness in stocks could threaten consumers' holiday gift-buying, if they feel less wealthy and less likely to spend.

Oxford Economics estimates that holiday retail sales will rise 4.2%, or an increase of 2.2% in volume after adjusting for inflation. That covers retail spending in November and December, excluding autos, gasoline, and bars and restaurants.

The National Retail Federation projects 182.7 million consumers plan to shop this year during the five-day Thanksgiving period that runs to "Cyber Monday", citing results from a recent survey. Black Friday is expected to be the most popular day to shop during that period. That overall number would be down slightly from 186.9 million last year, but continues the trend of elevated shopping during the holiday weekend in recent years, the NRF said.

Government data this week showed US retail sales for October increased moderately, while the core measure of such sales rose faster than expected. Retailers including Walmart ( WMT ) and Target ( TGT ) had upbeat comments or outlooks for the holiday season in their quarterly reports this week.

"The consumer is pretty healthy, and we'd like to see that continue through the end of the year," Nolte said.

COULD GASOLINE PRICES SAP SHOPPING?

Despite solid retail sales data, Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera Financial Group, said he was worried "that the consumer is being impacted by higher gas prices, higher energy prices, higher food prices."

The average national price for a gallon of gasoline stood at $3.69 on Friday, according to motorists' group AAA. That is down from about $4.28 a month ago, but well above the $3.10 level a year ago.

As the holiday shopping season heats up, Goldman said he was watching the extent of shopping done in stores compared to online, and how much consumers are buying necessities versus discretionary items.

"If the economy exceeds expectations, earnings increase, and earnings drive stock prices," Goldman said.

Investors in the coming week also will monitor reports on inflation and consumer confidence along with an updated read on third-quarter US GDP. Quarterly results are due from Dell Technologies ( DELL ) and semiconductor company Analog Devices ( ADI ) , which could sway the AI and tech trade.

With just over a month left in 2026, the S&P 500 is on track for a year-to-date gain of about 1%. The index has fallen for seven straight sessions, the longest such streak since February 2020. This week it dropped below its 200-day moving average -- a closely watched trendline that acts as a support level for buyers -- for the first time since April.

"There is a lot to like about the fundamentals" of the market, said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist for Nationwide. "But picking bottoms is difficult when the market is so emotional."

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf; Additional reporting by Saqib Iqbal Ahmed; editing by Colin Barr, David Gregorio and David Gaffen)

data.title: Bitcoin's quantum security challenge extends to bridges, custodians and millions of coins
data.description:
Bitcoin faces a problem that stronger cryptography alone cannot solve: moving millions of coins to quantum-resistant security while upgrading the exchanges, custodians and bridges that handle them.

Some blockchains have begun introducing quantum-resistant security. NEAR added post-quantum transaction signing in July, while Algorand introduced native Falcon-1024 accounts in August.

Millions of bitcoin (BTC) remain in wallets secured by older signatures, and exchanges, custodians and bridges would need to make their own changes to protect the funds they handle.

“The clock that matters is migration,” said Leo Fan, CEO of blockchain infrastructure company Cysic.

For bitcoin holders, moving funds to stronger security may become necessary long before quantum computers can break existing signatures. But dormant coins could remain exposed, and institutions holding or transferring bitcoin would have to upgrade their systems as well.

Exposed public keys

More than 6 million bitcoin, representing 31.2% of circulating supply, were held behind public keys already visible onchain in October, according to Glassnode data.

Those coins are safe for now, but a quantum computer powerful enough to break today's cryptography could use exposed public keys to gain control of the funds.

The figures illustrate the size of the migration challenge. They do not establish how many coins are lost, dormant or impossible to move.

Bitcoin developers are already debating what should happen to holdings that fail to migrate.

In April, developer Jameson Lopp and five co-authors proposed Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 361, which would phase out vulnerable signature methods and eventually restrict transactions from wallets that had not upgraded.

Lopp argued that freezing dormant bitcoin could be preferable to allowing future quantum attackers to steal it.

Blockstream CEO Adam Back favored voluntary upgrades, warning against forcing holders to migrate through a predetermined freeze.

Neither approach has been adopted. BIP 361 remains a draft, as does BIP 360, which proposes a new Bitcoin output type designed to reduce exposure to certain quantum attacks.

“Coins that never move are a social problem, not a technical one,” Fan said.

His concern is that developers can introduce new security standards, but they cannot necessarily compel wallet owners to adopt them.

“If the old path stays open forever, attackers will use it,” he said.

Bridges and custody

The same problem affects crypto custodians, which often require multiple parties to approve transactions rather than relying on a single private key. These systems would also need to be changed to support quantum-resistant signatures.

“Post-quantum signatures for a single signer are standardized, but threshold and multisig versions are still at the research stage,” Fan said.

The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology issued a call for multi-party threshold cryptography proposals in January, reflecting ongoing work.

In May, BitGo ( BTGO ) and Silence Laboratories completed a simulated post-quantum transaction using multi-party computation, a system that distributes control of private keys.

The demonstration showed how the technology could work in institutional custody, although the companies have not announced a production deployment.

Bridges connecting Bitcoin to other blockchains face similar complications because their security depends on systems operating across different networks.

Rootstock, a Bitcoin sidechain, has outlined plans to introduce quantum-resistant signatures in 2028. Its roadmap also includes changes to PowPeg, the bridge that secures bitcoin on Rootstock, and work on hardware security modules and Bitcoin-side protections.

Those changes remain proposals, and Rootstock cannot independently upgrade Bitcoin's underlying protocol.

For custodians and bridge operators, implementing new signatures will require changes to the systems that control funds, some of which depend on networks they do not operate.

For Bitcoin holders, the consequences could be more direct: those who cannot or do not migrate may eventually face restrictions on moving their coins, or leave them vulnerable to future attacks.

data.title: South Korea prepares market stabilisation funds after KOSPI hits 10-month low
data.description:
SEOUL, Nov 22 (Reuters) - South Korea will be ready to deploy market stabilisation funds immediately should conditions continue to deteriorate, the finance ministry said on Sunday, after the country's benchmark stock index slumped last week to a 10-month low.

"Preparation work on necessary measures... will immediately begin so that securities market stabilisation funds can be activated immediately depending on market conditions," the ministry said in a statement, after minister Lee Hyoung-il held an emergency meeting with other economic policymakers.

On Friday, the benchmark KOSPI stock index dropped more than 5% to close at its lowest level since January 16, as shares in Anthropic fizzled after their market debut amid general concerns about AI and tech valuations.

The Korean index has fallen more than 40% from its June peak after more than doubling in value in the first half in a world-beating rally, led by chipmakers Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF ) and SK Hynix ( SKHY ).

STABILISATION FUNDS

Among other market stabilising measures, the meeting attendees agreed to temporarily loosen for three months regulations on the daily limit of stock repurchases by listed companies, to help ease market volatility.

They also agreed to closely monitor leveraged investments and margin calls to ease selling pressure and respond to illegal short-selling and other market-disturbing behaviour.

The measures come after financial authorities in Taiwan on Saturday ordered a further tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while its finance ministry said its $15 billion stock stabilisation fund had already entered the market to support prices and maintain stability.

South Korea has rarely spent its securities market stabilising funds and has mostly used them as a tool to calm investor sentiment, including during the COVID-19 pandemic.

(Reporting by Jihoon Lee; Edting by Kate Mayberry and David Holmes)

data.title: Chinese exchanges ease margin trading requirements to aid stock markets
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov 22 (Reuters) - China's three main stock exchanges announced plans to aid struggling share prices with a batch of measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

In addition, the Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses unveiled plans for fee reductions to lower trading costs, while the Shenzhen exchange also proposed to introduce a market-making mechanism in its startup board ChiNext.

The moves came after Beijing unveiled measures in early November to encourage share purchases as equities struggle amid sluggish growth at home, a global selloff in AI stocks and rising geopolitical tensions.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index dropped nearly 3% last week to hit a 16-month low. Shanghai's tech-heavy STAR Market and Shenzhen's ChiNext have both tumbled more than 40% from their June peaks.

REGULATORY CHANGES

The Chinese measures come as other Asian markets including South Korea and Taiwan respond to stock market jitters with regulatory changes designed to steady volatility.

Under the new rules announced by the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges, investors can borrow more money to buy stocks against the same collateral.

Starting November 30, the minimum margin ratio would be cut to 80% from 100% previously, in a reversal of a policy announced in January.

"Margin financing activity has weakened significantly recently, while overall leverage is low," the three exchanges said in identical statements.

The cut in margin requirements "would improve market liquidity and support the market's long-term stability and healthy development."

MEASURES AIM TO BOOST MARKET CONFIDENCE

The level of China's outstanding margin loans has dropped more than 20% to roughly 2.2 trillion yuan ($329.49 billion), from a peak of 3 trillion yuan in late June.

Separately, the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges announced fee cuts aiming to lower trading costs, boost market confidence and invigorate the market.

The Shenzhen bourse also published draft rules to introduce market-making mechanisms in a bid to "curb share price swings, improve pricing efficiency and strengthen market resilience".

($1 = 6.6770 Chinese yuan renminbi)

(Reporting by Shanghai Newsroom; Editing by Tomasz Janowski and David Holmes)

data.title: Analysis-Correction or deeper reckoning? Investors seek signs US stock selling will abate
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Investors are scouring for signs that the steep US stock market selloff is nearing an end and leading to opportunities to buy beaten-up equities, but they remain concerned that negative momentum could drive the market into an even deeper slide.

Stocks tumbled again on Friday, ending the week sharply lower and sending the S&P 500 down 11.6% from its October 6 all-time high. That exceeds the 10% decline confirming a correction for the benchmark US stock index for the first time since March 2025, when trade tensions roiled markets.

For investors who have been conditioned to capitalize on declines during the four-year-old bull market, any signs of a potential market bottom could be a rare opportunity to buy at relatively cheap levels. As stocks sold off heavily on Friday, investors said some indicators were at least close to signaling a possible bottom, but they were wary of calling an end to the declines after a furious bout of selling. 

"Sentiment is very fragile at the moment," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones. "But ... there is a point where the drawdown is big enough to attract some buyers."

The market's six-week slide, featuring a steep fall for heavyweight technology shares, has come amid growing doubts about the AI trade, including mounting questions about the sustainability of heavy spending on data centers that has driven both profit and economic growth. The start of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes also has triggered anxiety about risk assets, investors said.

The S&P 500 as of Friday had fallen for seven straight sessions, its longest daily streak of declines since the onset of the coronavirus pandemic in 2020, while marking its biggest weekly drop in over a year. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite had lost its year-to-date gain, and was now down 2.7% in 2026. 

The selloff has reset valuations to more attractive levels, while weakening investor sentiment metrics to levels that often historically have been signals to buy, said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist for Nationwide.

However, Hackett said, "emotional investors can overwhelm opportunistic ones in the short term."

LOOKING FOR SIGNS IN MARKET INTERNALS

In the near term, analysts were turning to technical indicators, market internals and other metrics for signals of a possible bottom.

Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management, said he was watching the declines of individual S&P 500 stocks from their respective 52-week highs, and the extent to which stocks were moving in tandem -- with those metrics moving closer to oversold levels but not yet reaching extremes.

Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management, said one indicator -- which measures the relatively small number of New York Stock Exchange stocks at 52-week highs compared to those at lows -- was signaling a bottom. But a second one, the relatively low percentage above their 50-day moving averages, was close but had not yet signaled a market "washout," he said.

"We are getting close to a great dip-buying point," Zaro said.

Kourkafas said he was watching for moves below the market's surface. While consumer staples and other relatively defensive areas of the market, which often perform well in "risk off" environments, had recently shined, Kourkafas wanted to see strength in economically sensitive areas such as banks and industrials as indication that sentiment is stabilizing.

The Cboe Market Volatility index, which on Friday closed at 35.89, its highest level since the "Liberation Day" tariff tumult in April 2025, was also in focus for investors. When the VIX index has closed above 30 for the first time in a cycle, the S&P 500 has posted an average total return of 8.1% six months later, Kourkafas said.

Spikes in the volatility index, known as Wall Street's "fear gauge," could be a sign of extreme pessimism that paves the way for future gains.

Michael Reynolds, vice president of investment strategy at Glenmede, said the VIX was nearing the 40 level that could indicate "peak fear."

"There are some tell-tale signs we have a moment where the fear is detached from the strong fundamentals of earnings growth,"  Reynolds said.

FED MEETING, AI DEVELOPMENTS IN VIEW

US markets could see reduced trading volume in coming days, with fewer trading days next week due to the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.

The Fed's next rate-setting meeting on December 8-9 loomed as a potentially pivotal moment for markets. The US central bank is widely projected to raise rates by a standard quarter percentage point, but any signals for how many more hikes are expected this cycle will be crucial for stocks, Arone said. 

"Market participants are afraid that the Fed is tightening into an economic slowdown when both earnings and AI investment have peaked," Arone said. "Maybe a dovish hike would begin to soothe market fears."

Developments related to the outlook for AI investment also could be critical. While earnings season is largely done, results from semiconductor company Micron Technology ( MU ) on December 17 could have broad implications.

"There are many valuations that are still excessive.... This seems like a real correction which has further to go," said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder.

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf and Sinead Carew, additional reporting by Saqib Iqbal Ahmed, editing by Colin Barr and Diane Craft)

data.title: Exclusive-Like SpaceX, Anthropic ran an unusual IPO process, chafing some bankers
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 22 (Reuters) - For the second time this year, Wall Street bankers and lawyers took home a massive paycheck from a record-setting initial public offering. And for the second time this year, some of them came out of it complaining in private about how the process was riddled with complications and unlike any they had worked on before.

With SpaceX's IPO in June, in which banks earned half a billion dollars in fees, bankers chafed over how tightly the Elon Musk-led company controlled the months-long process and kept financial and other information private, making it hard for advisers to do their jobs. 

As Anthropic's IPO, dubbed internally "Project Lantern", eclipsed SpaceX on Thursday and bankers took home more than half a billion dollars in fees, several people close to the process listed a litany of problems that had plagued the offering process: a compressed timeline, marred by last-minute changes and delays in sharing financial projections; rushed document approvals; and highly unusual restrictions on bankers and concern about leaks - especially after Reuters reported many details from a draft IPO filing weeks before it was made public.

Anthropic, for example, instructed some of its 22 IPO underwriters to limit the number of bankers working on the deal to four, asking the firms to make sure they were senior staff, several people familiar with the matter said. One of the people said the restriction likely came out of fear that information would leak, and that the banks found a way to work around it anyway. 

Underlying these complaints is a new power dynamic between technology companies and Wall Street. Companies such as SpaceX, Anthropic - and potentially also OpenAI in the future -  have come to wield enormous power as the transformative potential of artificial intelligence creates a frenzied demand for their shares, and they are wielding it to do things their way. That is upsetting some bankers. But banks and investors appear to have little choice but to play along.

"These companies certainly did have some market power to tell underwriters that it's not going to be business as usual," said Jay Ritter, a University of Florida professor emeritus who researches IPOs. "But the big Wall Street firms, I suspect, are still going to be doing things as business as usual for all but maybe OpenAI (after these two deals)."

Ritter added that both SpaceX and Anthropic had negotiated to pay underwriters nothing on the additional shares sold through the greenshoe option. "I don't think most companies are going to be able to demand zero spread on overallotment shares," he said.

Anthropic, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley ( MS ), the two lead underwriters on the two IPOs, declined to comment.

SpaceX and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment.

Both SpaceX and Anthropic debuted successfully, raising record amounts of money, and their shares rallied initially. A key part of the underwriters' job is to market the securities. Thanks to the demand for AI, that was an easy sell - both companies had order books oversubscribed many times over. 

After an initial burst in shares, the trajectories of the two big AI firms diverged. SpaceX climbed to a post-listing peak of $201.80 on June 16 before retreating below its $135 IPO price for the first time in mid-July. Anthropic's shares closed down 8.5% on Friday after a 17% first-day pop, as a dramatic unraveling of the AI trade showed that even a blockbuster listing could not shake the gloom hanging over the sector.

UNUSUAL NON-COMPETES AND RESTRICTIONS

In the case of SpaceX's IPO, the people close to the process said Musk's team dictated terms at every stage. Musk's team told the largest and most powerful US banks - including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley ( MS ) - how to market SpaceX's stock and to whom. It told some banks the specific order sizes they needed to "fill" - in some cases a few billion dollars - and gave them instructions on what types of investors to bring. Banks signed on to underwrite the IPO without being told what they would be paid, the people said.

The underlying current running through Anthropic's IPO process was what several of the people who spoke to Reuters interpreted as a sense of extreme caution.    

Anthropic asked some senior officers at banks working on its IPO to sign legal documents restricting core members of the transaction team from working with rival companies, including OpenAI, Cursor, DeepSeek and Hugging Face, for six months after it went public, according to the people. 

Banks routinely manage conflicts and protect client confidentiality. But bankers and lawyers said it is rare for an IPO to impose exclusivity this broad, particularly on individual bankers. 

In previous head-to-head IPOs such as those of ridesharing rivals Uber ( UBER ) and Lyft ( LYFT ), or real estate companies Trulia and Zillow ( ZG ), banks could simply pick a side, in part because the deals were smaller and required fewer banks. 

Anthropic, by contrast, needed a broad syndicate to raise the enormous amount of capital it was seeking. That, some of the people said, explained why Anthropic sought to bind individual bankers with these restrictions. 

One banker who declined to sign on to the agreement said it was a challenge to find people who could promise not to actively cover or engage with Anthropic's peers, especially as several of those companies pursue their own initial or secondary offerings.  

INFORMATION LEAKS AND LATE NIGHTS 

Some of the restrictions were meant to control leaks of information. 

Nearly four weeks before Anthropic's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, called Form S-1, was made public, Reuters reported on it, revealing details of the company's financials, risk factors, dealings with other tech companies and other information. 

Anthropic also used a product called NetRoadshow to share information, instead of regular PDFs, with most of the banks underwriting the deal. 

NetRoadshow logs access details, including information such as who has seen the document and looked at which page. Documents on NetRoadshow also had individual bankers' names as watermarks. 

Leaks continued to surface in the press, but using NetRoadshow complicated bankers' work, including because the platform would not let them save copies of documents, one of the people said.

Anthropic planned to file an updated securities filing, called an S-1A, with the SEC with the price range and to launch the marketing on November 10. To do so, it needed to send a draft to all the banks in its syndicate for them to sign off on it.

The night before it was to happen, a law firm on the deal sent a PDF to the banks about the sale of shares in Canada. But soon it followed with another email asking them to disregard it, saying it "contains incorrect price range and share information," according to the email, which was seen by Reuters.  

The correct S-1A was then sent via the NetRoadshow platform around 2 a.m. New York time. Banks were told they had several hours to sign off on it before it was filed with the SEC. 

(Reporting by Echo Wang and Milana Vinn in New York; Editing by Paritosh Bansal, Jonathan Spicer and Muralikumar Anantharaman)

data.title: Washington governor, union denounce ICE arrests of travelers at Seattle airport
data.description:
Nov 21 - The governor of Washington state denounced federal immigration authorities on Saturday for arresting two people on a jetway at a Seattle-area airport.

The incident involving Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers occurred around 8 a.m. PST (1600 GMT) at the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport as people boarded an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles. ICE officers conducted an operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, who overstayed his visa, the agency said in a statement.

The officers also arrested a second individual, Sofia Hernandez Mejia, who threw hot coffee at them, ICE said in a post on social media. Mejia had also overstayed her visa, ICE said, adding that she would be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

Reuters was not able to identify lawyers for Mendoza or Mejia.

"ICE is completely and totally out of control and today we are confronted with yet more evidence of this," said Governor Bob Ferguson, a Democrat, at a news conference on Saturday.

Video of the incident circulated on social media and news outlets is "horrific" and "chilling," Ferguson said, adding that he told Alaska Airlines representatives that "they need to call on ICE to get out of our airports."

The governor said he would make the same request of every other airline that flies out of Sea-Tac airport.

Alaska Airlines said it is "concerned" by the federal action.

"Alaska Airlines was not provided advance notice of the enforcement action and we are working to understand the circumstances surrounding what occurred," the company said in a statement.

April Sims, president of the Washington State Labor Council, AFL-CIO, called the ICE arrest a "smash-and-grab" action that injected fear and chaos during a delicate time for air travel.

"Just days after our nation experienced widespread disruptions to air travel and flights being grounded, federal agents chose to carry out this operation at one of our busiest airports, during one the busiest travel weeks of the year," Sims said in a statement sent by the union, which includes local chapters representing flight attendants and ground crew at Sea-Tac airport.

Alaska Airlines said many passengers were put on other flights shortly after the incident and the originally scheduled flight departed at 11 a.m. PST (1900 GMT).

(Reporting by Dan Levine in San Francisco and Ryan Patrick Jones in Toronto; Editing by Sergio Non and Thomas Derpinghaus)

data.description:

By Chris Prentice and Alexandra Alper

NEW YORK/WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The US Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's ( NVDA ) accounting practices, said two people briefed on the matter, adding to the legal woes facing the scandal-hit chip giant.  

The Wall Street Journal on Tuesday reported that the SEC was probing Nvidia ( NVDA ) but said it could not ascertain the focus of the investigation. The people, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential issues, said SEC enforcement staff are scrutinizing potential accounting issues at the company.

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia ( NVDA ) did not immediately respond to requests for comment. 

Prices of Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares extended losses and were down about 13% on Friday, according to LSEG data, after Reuters reported details of the SEC probe. They had been down more than 6% before Reuters published its report.

Reuters could not immediately determine when the SEC opened its inquiry or exactly what potential accounting issues the watchdog is examining. Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action. 

Still, the accounting focus of the probe, which Reuters is reporting for the first time, increases pressure on Nvidia ( NVDA ), whose investors are still reeling from revelations about ousted CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital relationships, including with Alice Huang, who US authorities suspect is a Chinese spy. China has denied she is a spy.

Alice Huang led Singapore-based Megaspeed, historically a large Nvidia ( NVDA ) chip customer, people familiar with the matter have said. US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week. 

The crisis has sent shares in Nvidia ( NVDA ), a linchpin of the AI boom, tumbling more than a third and stoked calls in Washington for tougher action on tech threats posed by Beijing. 

Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and that it conducted "lawful business." Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name.

The SEC probe is the latest of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's ( NVDA ) $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported last month.

SINGAPORE ACCOUNTING CHANGE BACK IN FOCUS

Last year, Nvidia ( NVDA ) changed how it reports geographic revenue, using customer headquarters rather than billing addresses, which it said would better reflect the geographic profile of its revenue. The change resulted in Singapore being removed from its geographical breakdown. 

The Financial Times, citing company accounts, reported on Tuesday that Nvidia ( NVDA ) had made the change even as Singapore sales soared to almost half its global revenue. 

That accounting shift has drawn renewed press scrutiny in the wake of the Alice Huang scandal.

Southeast Asia has become a hub for chip smuggling to China since the Biden administration barred advanced AI chip exports to that country over concerns they could boost Beijing's military.

Analysts and investors have also grown increasingly concerned about circular AI financing deals, in which chipmakers including Nvidia ( NVDA ) have pursued complex financial arrangements to help customers fund purchases of their chips and the construction of costly AI infrastructure, such as data centers. Nvidia ( NVDA ) has backed AI companies and cloud providers and provided guarantees connected to data-center projects that use its equipment. 

Critics say such arrangements can make it harder for investors to assess the quality of chipmakers' revenue and their true financial exposure. Speaking to Reuters last month, SEC enforcement chief David Woodcock said the agency was examining AI companies' corporate disclosures to ensure issuers are giving investors the full picture on potential risks.

On its Tuesday earnings call, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) interim CEO and former CFO Colette Kress said the company was proud of its role in supporting the AI industry, but would be far more selective moving forward about AI industry financing deals. 

The SEC under President Donald Trump has pulled back on enforcement, saying it will focus on bread-and-butter securities fraud, including accounting violations that have long been a mainstay of its enforcement work. It recently launched a new financial reporting and accounting unit within its enforcement division, aimed at developing cases in accounting and auditing areas.

(Reporting by Chris Prentice in New York and Alexandra Alper in Washington; Additional reporting by Karen Freifeld and Jody Godoy in New York; Editing by Michelle Price and Daniel Wallis)

When paired with Autodesk Netfabb, users gain access to specialized additive manufacturing capabilities that help prepare, optimize, and process digital models for production.

data.title: Berkshire-owned utility lauds Oregon Supreme Court's expanded review of wildfire lawsuit
data.description:
Nov 21 (Reuters) - Berkshire Hathaway's ( BRK/A ) PacifiCorp utility said on Saturday it welcomed a decision by the Oregon Supreme Court to look into all potential errors in the handling of a wildfire class-action against the company.

Oregon residents and business owners who want PacifiCorp to be held liable for four wildfires in 2020 hope to reverse a state appeals court's decision that wiped out $1.25 billion of awards to 201 plaintiffs because of an error with the instructions to jurors.

But the state's highest court on Friday expanded its review of the case to include all possible errors raised in the appeal, not just the jury instructions. That may increase the possibility that the state Supreme Court will find problems in the trial judge's handling of the litigation, including whether he should have certified a class to begin with.

Friday's decision means Portland-based PacifiCorp will not face additional so-called mini-trials over its liability to fire victims while the appeals process continues.

"The Court recognizes the litany of missteps in this case, and we remain confident that sound legal principles and facts will prevail," Ryan Flynn, president of PacifiCorp's Pacific Power division, said in a statement released on Saturday.

Attorneys for the plaintiffs did not immediately comment on the order.

If plaintiffs win the lawsuit, PacifiCorp could face tens of billions of dollars in potential damages over its role in the 2020 wildfires.

More than 2,400 plaintiffs blamed the Portland-based utility's equipment and alleged negligent failure to shut down power lines during a Labor Day weekend windstorm for damaging more than 2,000 properties. The state's high court heard oral arguments in the case earlier this month.

The appeals court's decision focused on the jury instruction by Multnomah County Circuit Court Judge Steffan Alexander, and not whether a class action was justified.

Friday's order set deadlines in early 2027 for the parties to file briefs on the broader set of appellate issues.

(Reporting by Dan Levine in San Francisco and Jonathan Stempel in New York; Editing by Sergio Non and Matthew Lewis)

NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US stocks extended their rout on Friday, and the S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections after Anthropic's momentous debut fell flat, exacerbating worries about the AI trade that has driven this year's stock market rally.

All three major US equity indexes ended sharply lower. The Dow and the S&P 500 are now more than 10% below their record closing highs, confirming both indexes have entered a correction.

The bellwether S&P 500 notched its seventh consecutive drop, its longest losing streak since February 2020.

The S&P 500 and the Dow logged their largest weekly percentage losses since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced his market-rattling "liberation day" tariff package.

The Nasdaq's weekly drop was its largest since March 2020. The tech-heavy index has dipped into negative territory for the year.

"This is clearly a challenging day for capital markets, and as we head into a Friday close, appears to be accelerating to a certain degree," said Bill Northey, senior investment director at US Bank Wealth Management in Billings, Montana. "But as we step back and evaluate fundamentals and sentiment, sentiment is clearly winning the day today."

"Sentiment is always the more powerful force in the immediate space, whereas fundamentals tend to win out over time," Northey added, referring to economic strength and solid corporate earnings, among other things.

Anthropic's supersized debut as a publicly held company, which was intended to raise as much as $2 trillion in market cap, failed to catch fire on Thursday, closing 17.1% above its $83 offer price as enthusiasm for the stock faded throughout the session.

In its second day as a publicly held company, Anthropic's shares fell 9.1%. Nvidia's shares tumbled 13.8%.

The Anthropic IPO, combined with Nvidia's quarterly earnings report, failed to dispel fears over risks associated with artificial intelligence and the massive expenditures on the nascent technology.

"Nvidia reported what might have been one of the greatest quarters in corporate earnings history; they did everything right," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana. "A lot of people, myself included, were looking to the Anthropic debut to some extent as a clearing event, and it wasn't."

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index , which has powered much of the broader stock market's gains in recent months, was up as much as 106.6% in mid-June. That luster has faded, with the index's year-to-date advance having shrunk to 18.7%.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon fell 3.9%, while Meta dropped 5.9%.

Neocloud firm CoreWeave fell 12.1% and its peer Nebius slid 16.1%.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48,147.33, the S&P 500 lost 265.41 points, or 3.70%, to 6,910.42 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 1,261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22,617.73.

The CBOE Market Volatility Index , often referred to as Wall Street's "fear gauge," rose to its highest close since April 7, 2025.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the central bank's policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels.

Markets are pricing a near-certain likelihood of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 12.8% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

UnitedHealth rose 2.8% after TD Cowen upgraded its shares to a "buy" from a "hold" rating.

The AI selloff also sent Caterpillar 5% lower on worries over weakening demand for its power-generating and backup power equipment.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

Taiwan's index fell 4.6% in a single week. Learn to read the charts behind moves like these with the free Stock Preachers guide, plus The Roadmap market reports, at stockpreachers.com.

data.title: Update: AI Worries Send S&P 500 Into Correction Territory as Nasdaq Turns Negative For The Year
data.description:
05:15 PM EST, 11/20/2026 (MT Newswires) -- (Updates with market moves at the end of the day, and other changes, if any.)

The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average entered correction territory Friday, while the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year amid mounting skepticism around stocks linked to artificial intelligence.

The S&P 500 tumbled 3.7% to 6,910.39, extending its losing streak to a seventh consecutive session. The Dow dipped 1.9% to 48,147.33, marking its fifth day of decline.

A 10% stock pullback from recent highs is considered the minimum threshold for a market correction. Investors are concerned about the durability of the AI boom amid soaring valuations.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq plummeted 5.3% to 22,617.73, logging two back-to-back losses. The index is now down 2.7% this year.

Except consumer staples, all sectors ended in the red, led by tech's 7.1% slump.

This week, the Nasdaq shed 10%, while the S&P 500 slid 8.6%. The Dow recorded a weekly loss of 8%.

"The strength of the AI buildout has now spread wide enough that its end -- and we're certainly not saying that is now -- would likely trigger a broader bear market in equities, a downturn in the US economy and reversal of (Federal Reserve) policy," said Robert Kavcic, senior economist at BMO.

Anthropic's (ANT) shares tumbled 8.5%, having surged 17% in the previous session following a record Nasdaq debut. The Claude AI chatbot maker said Friday it completed its upsized initial public offering, raising about $93.5 billion.

"The ANT got squished (and) took the whole AI trade down with it," Scotiabank said in a note.

Tech bellwether Nvidia ( NVDA ) slid 14%, the worst performer on the Dow and among the steepest declines on the S&P 500. The Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into Nvidia's ( NVDA ) accounting practices, Reuters reported, citing two people briefed on the matter.

Major chipmakers such as Intel ( INTC ) , Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) , Qualcomm ( QCOM ) , Micron Technology ( MU ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) fell sharply. Shares of AI hyperscalers including Microsoft ( MSFT ) , Amazon ( AMZN ) and Meta Platforms ( META ) also declined.

Treasury yields declined, with the two-year rate down 13 basis points at 4.65% and the 10-year rate falling 10.2 basis points to 4.95%.

Inflation in the US continues to be "unacceptably high" and the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike in September is unlikely to help ease price pressures, Fed Governor Lisa Cook said Friday.

US consumer sentiment improved in November, led by "substantial" increases in expected business conditions following the midterm elections, while the year-ahead inflation outlook reached its lowest level since February, a survey by the University of Michigan showed.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil edged up 0.9% to $83.98 a barrel, while Brent rose 0.6% to $92.50 a barrel.

China is set to overtake the US as the world's largest oil consumer by around 2034 as Washington navigates an economic slowdown and benefits from fuel efficiency gains, Oxford Economics said in a note.

Spot gold fell 2.4% to $3,538.49 per troy ounce, while silver shed 7.5% to $41.52 per ounce.

Making Human Movement Visible with AI Vision

Using camera-based visual input and AI algorithms, the system enables three key capabilities: human detection, skeletal keypoint detection, and real-time motion tracking.

The system first identifies individuals within the camera frame, then detects and connects key body points to generate a skeletal representation of human posture. By tracking these keypoints across consecutive video frames, it can continuously analyze changes in body position and movement patterns.

The processed motion data is translated into intuitive visualizations and displayed on large screens, allowing users to see their movements reflected digitally in real time. Demonstration scenarios include common physical activities such as squats, vertical jumps, and high knees, showcasing the system's ability to recognize and visualize different human movements.

data.title: ModuleMD Continues to Strengthen Its Position in Allergy EHR Innovation with a New Generation of AI-Powered Technology

Following strong client interest in its new WISE Touch AI experience, ModuleMD showcases its expanding technology ecosystem at ACAAI 2026, bringing clinical intelligence, automated workflows and specialty-focused innovation together for allergy practices.

PHOENIX, Nov. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --  Allergy practices are facing a new set of expectations. Clinical documentation needs to move faster. Front-office teams are managing increasingly complex administrative workflows. Patients expect greater transparency, while practices need technology that understands the demands of specialty care.

For more than 25 years, ModuleMD has built its technology around these realities. At the 2026 American College of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology (ACAAI) Annual Scientific Meeting in Phoenix, Arizona, the company brought that commitment into focus, showcasing a new generation of AI-powered capabilities designed to advance how allergy and immunology practices deliver care and manage their operations.

At Booth #1713, the conversation centered on the continued development of the ModuleMD EHR platform, particularly its latest WISE Touch AI experience. The showcase also highlighted innovations in automated skin testing, clinical documentation, conversational practice intelligence and AI-powered front-office operations.

The momentum extends beyond the conference floor. Following its recent WISE Touch first-look webinar, ModuleMD has seen considerable interest and positive feedback from existing clients, reflecting growing enthusiasm for an EHR experience designed around the way specialty practices actually work.

An EHR Built Around Allergy. Now, With AI at Its Core.

Specialty healthcare technology requires more than a general-purpose EHR with a few specialty features added to it. Allergy practices have distinct clinical, operational and revenue cycle requirements, from immunotherapy and skin testing to biologics management and recurring patient workflows.

ModuleMD's approach has been to build around these requirements from the ground up.

Its latest development, WISE Touch AI, brings a redesigned clinical experience and multiple AI-powered capabilities into one connected platform. Rather than treating artificial intelligence as a separate application, ModuleMD is integrating it into the everyday work of clinicians and practice teams.

The result is an EHR experience built around three important areas: clinical productivity, administrative automation and access to practice intelligence.

A redesigned clinical experience brings AI-assisted documentation, clinical decision support and CPT suggestions closer to the point of care. Designed around simpler interactions and fewer manual steps, WISE Touch AI aims to reduce the administrative effort involved in documenting and managing patient encounters.

AI-powered clinical documentation with JOSH™ takes this further. JOSH converts natural conversations into structured clinical notes, helping clinicians spend less time typing and more time with patients. Supporting more than 75 languages, the technology brings conversational documentation into the clinical workflow.

ModuleMD Front Desk extends AI into practice operations through five specialized agents working across patient intake, scheduling, insurance eligibility and estimates, authorizations and referrals, coordinated by a supervisor agent. The objective is to reduce repetitive administrative work while keeping essential front-office processes connected.

ModuleMDQ™ adds another dimension through conversational practice intelligence. Instead of navigating multiple screens to locate information, practice teams can interact with their practice data using natural language and get answers that help them move work forward.

Together, these capabilities reflect a broader direction for the ModuleMD EHR: clinical workflows, administrative operations and practice intelligence working as one system.

Rethinking Skin Testing Through AI

Innovation at ModuleMD also extends into some of the most specific workflows in allergy care.

Skin testing remains a fundamental part of allergy diagnostics, but measuring and documenting wheal and flare reactions can involve repetitive manual effort. ModuleMD's SkinSight™ technology introduces image-based AI measurement into this process.

Using images captured on a device already available to the practice, SkinSight detects and measures wheal and flare reactions, with structured results and timestamped images transferred directly into the patient's chart.

The integration of measurement, documentation and clinical records helps reduce manual data entry while giving clinicians the ability to review and interpret results. It also supports documentation for CPT 95004.

Developed with allergy-specific workflows in mind, SkinSight reflects an important distinction in ModuleMD's approach to AI: technology should address actual clinical tasks, not simply introduce another layer of software.

Client Interest Signals a New Chapter for the ModuleMD EHR

Product innovation is only meaningful when it makes a difference to the people using it.

ModuleMD's recent WISE Touch first-look webinar gave existing clients an opportunity to explore the new clinical experience and its connected AI capabilities. The response reflected strong interest in the direction of the platform, particularly the opportunity to bring clinical documentation, front-office automation and practice intelligence closer together.

For ModuleMD, this engagement is part of an ongoing relationship with the specialty practices that use its technology every day.

The company continues to develop its EHR around client needs, evolving clinical workflows and the operational realities of independent specialty practices. That means looking beyond individual features to how different parts of a practice work together.

The objective isn't simply to add more functionality. It is to make the technology more useful at every point where clinicians and their teams interact with it.

More Than an EHR: A Connected Platform for Allergy Practices

ModuleMD's platform brings together Electronic Health Records, Practice Management, Patient Engagement, Revenue Cycle Management, Allergy Immunotherapy, Biologics and Infusion Management.

This connected foundation is particularly important for allergy practices, where clinical care and practice operations are closely linked. From patient encounters and skin testing to immunotherapy workflows, biologics administration and revenue cycle management, the technology needs to support the full operational picture.

With more than 25 years of specialty healthcare experience, continued investment in AI and a platform shaped by the needs of its clients, ModuleMD is building on its position in allergy-focused healthcare technology.

Its presence at ACAAI 2026 offered a closer look at that direction: an EHR that continues to develop, AI that works within real practice workflows, and technology designed with the specific demands of allergy care at its center.

As specialty healthcare moves toward more connected and intelligent systems, ModuleMD's focus remains on making technology work better for the practices that depend on it.

ModuleMD. One Practice. One Platform

data.description:
* Youth Congress workers storm Meta offices in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Gurugram

* Protesters want leaders' Instagram accounts restored; two have been, many remain curbed

* Meta restricted over 5.4 million items in India in first half of 2026

(Tweaks lede, adds details of Congress Delhi protest banner, opposition reactions in paragraph 8, 10)

NEW DELHI, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The youth wing of India's main opposition Congress party on Saturday warned of more protests against Meta's removal of some accounts and posts of its members, a day after clashing with police outside the US firm's India offices.

Meta declined to comment on Friday's unprecedented protests, which marked an escalation by the influential political group in the company's biggest market by users. Debate is growing in India about potential risks to free speech from the increasingly strict efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government to remove social media content it objects to.

Modi's government says it orders content to be taken down only if it breaches local laws, can harm public safety or national security. Congress has long accused Meta and other social media platforms of curbing dissent online by removing party accounts, favouring Modi's government.

Meta has said it restricts content in India to comply with local laws.

In Hyderabad on Friday, protesters carrying placards chanted slogans as they stormed into the building that houses Meta's offices, smashing plants to the ground and clashing with police, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress' X account.

Another video showed Congress workers spray-painting anti-Meta slogans on walls outside the building that houses its Mumbai office, clashing with security guards who tried to stop them. In Gurugram near New Delhi, Congress workers chanted slogans and held banners reading "restore youth Congress accounts", official online posts showed.

The Indian Youth Congress posted warnings on X that it would "storm your offices across the country and stage protests" unless Instagram accounts of its leaders are restored.

On Saturday, the Congress wing posted a video of its workers putting up a banner in central Delhi taking a dig at Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, referring to him as "Mark BJPberg" to allege the company's favouritism towards Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.

India's IT ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

MODI'S PARTY ACCUSES CONGRESS OF VANDALISM

Telangana opposition politician K.T. Rama Rao criticised Congress workers over what he called vandalism at Meta's Hyderabad office, saying it had undermined the city's reputation as a safe destination for businesses.

Pradeep Bhandari, a national spokesperson for Modi's ruling party, criticised Congress' actions on Saturday, saying they had "not only vandalised and destroyed Meta's office in Hyderabad" but were also "flaunting it on social media".

"This is Congress Model: Vandalise offices of Private companies," he wrote.

Two such accounts were restored after Friday's protests, but thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted, Manu Jain, who is in charge of social media for the youth group, told Reuters on Saturday.

Meta must explain how its algorithms restrict posts and must restore accounts taken down on government orders, he added.

Reporters Without Borders has said the removal of journalistic content from social media has been on the rise in India this year, and free speech activists say a new government rule gives social media companies hardly any time to review and decide on takedown requests.

In February, Modi's government ordered social media companies to take down unlawful content within three hours of being notified about it, tightening an earlier 36-hour timeline.

Meta disclosures show that it restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, second only to Indonesia and up from about 70,000 in the whole of 2025.

"The large majority of these items included instances where we were obligated to proactively restrict content... based on local law requirements," Meta said.

(Reporting by Aditya Kalra and Munsif Vengattil; Editing by William Mallard)

data.title: Persona Earns CEN/TS 18099 High Certification for Injection Attack Detection
data.description:
Independent evaluation of Persona's Android SDK confirms defenses against deepfakes and other injected media at the top level of the first standard

SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Persona, the leading global identity platform, today announced that its Android SDK has earned CEN/TS 18099 High certification for injection attack detection (IAD). High certification  is the top level of the European standard. The evaluation was run by CLR CERT, the certification body of Cabinet Louis Reynaud (CLR) Labs. CLR Labs is accredited under ISO/IEC 17025, the international standard for testing laboratories, and it edits CEN/TS 18099. This certificated injection attack detection is available to all Persona customers and can be activated by working with Persona's team.

Injection attacks skip the camera entirely. Instead of holding a photo or mask up to a lens, fraudsters use virtual cameras, emulators and tampered devices to feed stolen, manipulated, or AI-generated media straight into the verification flow. To the system, the result looks like a real live capture, and traditional liveness checks aren't built to catch it.

"Our customers are facing more sophisticated deepfakes, face swaps and replay attacks while their identity verification volumes grow rapidly," said Irfan Faizullabhoy, product manager at Persona. "Earning CEN/TS 18099 High is one way we're helping them stay ahead of both, with independently tested defenses that work at scale."

A demanding, independent evaluation

The European Committee for Standardization (CEN) published CEN/TS 18099 in 2024 as the first standard for testing injection attack detection. It grades systems at three levels: Basic, Substantial and High. To test at the High level, evaluators spent at least 30 person-days attacking Persona's Android SDK. They used at least three injection methods, including rooted devices, tampered camera services and custom operating system builds. They also used at least 15 types of attack media, including deepfake videos, AI-generated faces and spliced video clips. Evaluators checked that real users could still verify, so a system couldn't pass just by blocking everyone.

"CLR CERT congratulates Persona on achieving High-level compliance under the CLR CERT IAD certification program for CEN/TS 18099," said Kévin Carta, director of CLR Labs. "As editor of the European standard on biometric injection attacks, we built this evaluation to test defenses against injected video, tampered apps, and modified operating systems. In a constantly changing digital world, compliance is more essential than ever. We are honored that Persona selected CLR CERT."

Built for fraud teams, invisible to real users

Persona's injection attack defenses run automatically and in real time. Users take a short guided selfie while Persona analyzes video, device and camera signals in the background to confirm a live person is in front of a real camera. Fraud and risk teams get clear reason codes, such as "virtual camera detected," so they can explain each decision during audits and appeals.

"Deepfake submissions keep growing in volume and sophistication, but agentic AI is an even more alarming trend," said Daniel Lee, product lead at Persona. "We're seeing more real-time phishing attacks where bad actors mimic verification flows, trick people into submitting their government IDs and selfies and then try to inject that genuine media into legitimate sessions. That makes detecting and stopping injection attacks more critical than ever."

Meeting the EU's rising bar for remote identity proofing

The certification comes as the EU tightens its rules for remote identity proofing. The EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation, which covers remote customer identification, applies from July 10, 2027. European identity-proofing standards, including ETSI TS 119 461 for trust service providers, already point to CEN/TS 18099 testing.

Persona's certification is listed on the CLR CERT certified products list at clr-cert.eu/produits_certifies. To learn more, visit: https://withpersona.com/blog/persona-achieves-cen-ts-18099-high-certification 

Customers can turn on certified injection attack detection by contacting their Persona account team.

About Persona

Persona is an identity platform that helps organizations keep the internet safer and more accessible for real people and businesses. Organizations use Persona to securely collect, verify, manage and make decisions about the identities of individuals, businesses and agents, with AI-backed orchestration that automates and streamlines the process from end to end. Backed by Persona’s own research into emerging threats, its fraud prevention and identity theft protection have stopped more than 300 million fraud attempts, including synthetic identities, account takeovers and deepfakes.

Founded in 2018 and headquartered in San Francisco, Persona has verified roughly 1 billion identities and is available in more than 200 countries and territories and 20 languages. Persona supports consumer-facing businesses across a variety of sectors, including LinkedIn, OpenAI, Twilio, Square, Udemy, Travelex and Gusto. For more information, visit withpersona.com.

data.title: EU leaders' chair proposes new cuts to EU 2028-2034 budget draft, suggests digital tax
data.description:
* Costa proposes 3% digital tax on online advertising and intermediation turnover

* Proposal cuts seven-year EU budget by €40 billion to €1.582 trillion versus October draft

* EU leaders discuss plan on November 26 to 27 aiming for December agreement

By Jan Strupczewski

BRUSSELS, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The chairman of European Union leaders proposed further cuts to the European Commission's draft EU 2028-2034 budget on Saturday and suggested new revenue streams for the EU, including a digital tax, to help finance EU policies.

The cuts proposed by Antonio Costa, who chairs summits of EU leaders, would reduce the overall seven-year budget by €40 billion to €1.582 trillion compared to a proposal presented by the Irish EU presidency in October and by €180.6 billion compared to the original Commission proposal.

Costa's proposal mainly cuts the European Competitiveness Fund - aimed at helping make European industry more competitive against China and the United States - defence and external spending. Money for agriculture and cohesion is relatively protected compared to the Irish compromise proposal.

Nevertheless, France criticised the new numbers as not sufficiently protecting farmers, and the European Parliament's chief budget negotiator, Siegfried Muresan, said the numbers were a step backwards.

"This proposal is unacceptable to Parliament and cannot form the basis for our consent. The EU budget is an investment budget. Cuts, more cuts and a side of cuts are not an investment strategy," he said.

EU leaders will discuss Costa's proposals at a special summit on November 26-27 with a view to narrowing differences between the EU budget's net contributors and net beneficiaries, and to reaching an agreement in December.

The EU budget is how the 27-member bloc finances all its policies - from supporting farmers to developing new technology and supporting industry and research against competition from China and the US.

It also covers student exchanges, equalising standards of living across the EU, help for Ukraine and EU officials' salaries, among others.

DIGITAL TAX A PROPOSED NEW REVENUE

The EU budget is financed from national contributions and the so-called "own resources" - taxes and levies that are collected by EU countries but are dedicated to the EU budget, such as customs duties, a percentage of value-added taxes or a tax on non-recycled plastic waste.

The more such "own resources" the EU budget has, the less governments have to contribute from national coffers.

Costa's proposal for the digital tax builds on a 2018 proposal by the European Commission that was not taken up by EU governments at the time.

Costa has now proposed that the EU put a 3% tax on the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data for companies with an annual turnover for digital activities of €50 million in the EU and a global turnover of over €750 million.

This would mean taxing mostly US-based digital giants such as Google, Microsoft ( MSFT ), Meta, Apple or Amazon ( AMZN ), a move many EU governments have been wary of for fear of angering US President Donald Trump, who has spoken against such a tax.

To find more money, Costa proposed slowing down the repayment of the capital of the more than €600 billion that the EU will have jointly borrowed by the end of 2026 for its post-pandemic recovery fund.

The repayment of the interest and capital will start in 2028 and last until 2058 as initially planned, but the repayment of capital may be slower in the first seven years to leave more money in the budget for other priorities, officials said.

The budget and its sources of revenue must be agreed unanimously and it is often an acrimonious battle. The seven-year ​2028-2034 budget under discussion now is particularly difficult because of additional pressures on national ⁠budgets from high energy prices and defence spending.

Although the EU budget only has to be ready for 2028, leaders want a deal by the end of 2026 because there are elections next year in France, Italy, Poland, Greece, Estonia, ⁠Finland ​and Slovakia, with the budget likely to play a role in electoral ​campaigns.

(Editing by Timothy Heritage)

data.title: Entain in talks to sell remainder of CEE business to CVC, Sky News reports
data.description:
Nov 21 (Reuters) - Ladbrokes owner Entain ( GMVHF ) is in advanced talks to sell its remaining stake in its central and eastern Europe operations to private equity firm CVC Capital Partners in a deal that could value the division at between £1.5 billion and £1.75 billion ($1.96 billion to $2.29 billion), Sky News reported on Saturday, citing sources.

Here are some details:

* Entain ( GMVHF ) holds a 47.5% stake in the CEE business, having offloaded a 20% interest to joint venture partner EMMA Capital in June for €425 million ($466.1 million)

* Entain ( GMVHF ) said at the time it would keep evaluating options to fully exit the business, which owns SuperSport in Croatia and STS in Poland

* According to Sky, there are other interested parties

* Entain ( GMVHF ) is under pressure to cut costs to offset increases in Britain's gambling taxes. It expects an extra £25 million hit to its UK and Ireland retail business after the government raised taxes on the industry for a second consecutive year in last month's budget

* Entain ( GMVHF ) declined to comment on the report, while CVC did not immediately respond to a request for comment sent outside regular business hours

($1 = 0.7645 pounds)

($1 = 0.9118 euros)
